text: On the SciQ testbed, we evaluated a contrastive pretext objective applied before weak-label fine-tuning, using 1000 pretext steps and 16 seeds. The measured performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.78 with a standard error of 0.12. No baseline PGR was supplied in the provided data, so this number cannot be positioned as an improvement over, or a regression from, any comparison condition; it should be read only as the absolute level attained by this configuration. The standard error of 0.12 across the 16 seeds indicates appreciable seed-to-seed spread, so the point estimate should be treated as approximate rather than tightly pinned down. We also lack information on other hyperparameters, on how PGR was computed, and on whether the pretext step count was tuned, all of which limit what can be inferred. Replication with an explicit baseline arm and a sweep over pretext_steps would be needed to assess whether the contrastive stage contributes anything.
